name: Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor with Perineurial Differentiation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for MPNST with Perineurial Differentiation

criteria.description: Presence of spindle cell sarcoma with areas showing perineurial cell differentiation
Positive staining for perineurial markers such as EMA (epithelial membrane antigen) and claudin-1
MRI showing a soft tissue mass along peripheral nerves with heterogeneous enhancement
Rapidly enlarging painful mass along a peripheral nerve distribution

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of spindle cell sarcoma with perineurial differentiation and positive immunohistochemical staining for perineurial markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other spindle cell sarcomas and confirmation of perineurial differentiation by immunohistochemistry.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neuropathic pain localized to affected nerve distribution
Electrophysiological evidence of nerve conduction block

searchTerms: difficulty moving affected arm or leg

common.symptomName: Sensory deficits including numbness or paresthesia
searchTerms: pins and needles in affected area

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy distal to tumor site
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in limb

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction such as sweating abnormalities
searchTerms: issues with sweating and autonomic system
open skin wound on tumor site
swollen lymph nodes from cancer spread
shortness of breath due to lung tumors

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
Non-specific inflammatory markers may be elevated
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with nerve involvement
CT scan for assessment of metastasis
other: Histopathology demonstrating spindle cells with perineurial differentiation
Immunohistochemical positivity for EMA, claudin-1, and GLUT1

distinguishingFeatures: S100 protein strongly positive without perineurial marker expression
Slow growth and absence of malignant features
Typically arises near joints rather than along nerves

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging painful mass along a peripheral nerve
New onset neurological deficits in affected limb
Skin ulceration or necrosis over tumor
references: Stacchiotti S, et al. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors: diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Expert Rev Anticancer Ther. 2016.
Miettinen M, et al. Perineurial differentiation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors: a clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical study. Am J Surg Pathol. 2015.
Orphanet: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with perineurial differentiation (ORPHA:252128)
